sections.html:
Gloucester County is on the lower Middle Peninsula, with the York River on its south side and the Chesapeake Bay to the east. The county seat is Gloucester Courthouse, and the county is part of the Virginia Beach-Norfolk-Newport News metropolitan area, about 60 miles east of Richmond.

It covers 288 square miles, but only 218 are land, since about 24 percent of the total area is water. Buyers often ask about the water, so expect questions about flooding and insurance.

It borders Middlesex, Mathews, York, James City and King and Queen counties. The George P. Coleman Memorial Bridge carries U.S. 17 over the York River to York County and the Peninsula.

sections.h2: What is the history behind Gloucester County?
sections.html:
The county was formed in 1651 from York County and named for Henry Stuart, Duke of Gloucester, a son of Charles I. The site of Werowocomoco, the capital of the Powhatan Confederacy, lies on the north side of the York River here, and archaeologists confirmed the village site in 2003.

Tobacco farming drove the colonial economy, and several plantation houses still stand, including Rosewell and Warner Hall. Gloucester Point, at the narrow crossing of the York River, was fortified in the 1660s and again in later wars.

One piece of local geography has its own name. The area called Guinea, near Gloucester Point, includes Achilles, Maryus, Perrin, Severn and Big Island, and it was long the center of the county's seafood trade.

Old Gloucester deeds can reference parishes and landmarks that no longer exist, so a seller with an inherited parcel should ask the Circuit Court clerk to pull the chain of title early.

Farmland, the waterfront and a commuter link to the Peninsula all matter. Wikipedia describes Gloucester as a retail center around its Main Street and U.S. 17, and as a county that kept large rural areas in the north.

The Virginia Employment Commission list reproduced on Wikipedia names these among the largest employers: Gloucester County Public Schools, Riverside Regional Medical Center, the Virginia Institute of Marine Science, Rappahannock Community College, Walmart and the County of Gloucester. That list is dated, so treat it as a pointer, not a current ranking.

The Virginia Institute of Marine Science, the graduate marine school of William & Mary, is at Gloucester Point on the York River.

sections.h2: How does climate and water affect a Gloucester County house?
sections.html:
With about a quarter of the county's area under water, many parcels sit near tidal creeks, marsh or river frontage.

Storm history is part of the record. Page Middle School was damaged by a tornado on April 16, 2011, and the school was rebuilt across the street in 2015.

  • Check for moisture in crawl spaces and under porches on low lots.
  • Ask about the age of the septic system and well on rural parcels.
  • Keep any receipts for roof or drainage repairs, because a buyer will ask.

sections.h2: Which schools and parks do buyers mention in Gloucester County?
sections.html:
Gloucester County Public Schools has nine schools: five elementary (Abingdon, Achilles, Bethel, Botetourt and Petsworth), two middle schools (Peasley and Page) and Gloucester High School.

Parks include Beaverdam Park, which sits on a reservoir with trails and boat rental, Woodville Park, Gloucester Point Beach Park and Tyndall's Point Park. The annual Daffodil Festival is held the first weekend in April, and the county calls itself the Daffodil Capital of the World.

sections.h2: Who handles real estate tax in Gloucester County?
sections.html:
The Department of Real Estate Assessment sets values, and the Treasurer collects. The assessment office is at 6489 Main Street, Suite 126, and its number is 804-693-1325. The Treasurer's number is 804-693-2141.

The county says real estate is assessed at 100 percent of fair market value and must be reassessed every three years. Its document list includes a 2026 reassessment and a 2023 reassessment, and the county's staff also lists and appraises new construction from building permits.

The county's own page says assessors use mass appraisal, and that the department does not set market values but reacts to sales and market changes.

sections.h2: When are Gloucester County real estate taxes due?
sections.html:
Real estate tax is billed in two installments, due June 30 and December 5. For 2026 the second installment moved to December 7 because December 5 falls on a weekend.

  • Early June: first installment bills mailed.
  • June 30: first installment due.
  • July 1: 10 percent penalty applies to unpaid first installment bills, and 10 percent annual interest starts.
  • Early November: second installment bills mailed.
  • December 5 (December 7 in 2026): second installment due, with penalty after the due date.

The Treasurer's page puts the 2026 rate at $0.583 per $100 of assessed value. Taxes may be paid in full by June 30, and if a mortgage company escrows your tax, the property owner stays responsible for making sure it is paid.

The county also offers e-billing through an enrollment portal described on the Treasurer's page.

sections.h2: How do you appeal a Gloucester County assessment?
sections.html:
First ask for an administrative review from the Real Estate Assessment office. The owner or an authorized agent files the county's application by the deadline printed on the reassessment notice.

If the review does not settle it, you can file an application with the Board of Equalization, a five-member citizen board appointed by the Circuit Court. The county notes owners may go straight to the board, but most differences are settled at the department level. The last step is a petition to the Circuit Court, and the county gives the Clerk's number as 804-693-2502.

Elderly and disabled tax relief is run through the Commissioner of the Revenue, with an application window that runs from February 1 to May 1. The Commissioner's number is 804-693-3451.

sections.h2: What happens to unpaid tax in Gloucester County?
sections.html:
The Treasurer publishes delinquent lists, and real estate with tax owing for more than two years as of December 31 is subject to sale at public auction under the Virginia Code's bill in equity process. The county names Taxing Authority Consulting Services, P.C. as a firm handling that work.

For a seller, the Virginia Code puts the real estate tax lien ahead of every other lien until the taxing authority is paid, and the lien statute includes penalties and interest. The closing agent pays the balance from your proceeds, so ask the Treasurer for a payoff figure before closing.

sections.h2: What do sellers in Gloucester County usually face?
sections.html:
Owners here often hold inherited waterfront or rural parcels, older homes needing repairs, or houses with tax that slipped past the June 30 or December 5 due dates.

We buy houses as-is in Gloucester County, and the title company pays unpaid real estate tax from the proceeds.

faqs.q: What is the 2026 real estate tax rate in Gloucester County?
faqs.a: The Treasurer's page lists $0.583 per $100 of assessed value for 2026. Real estate is assessed at 100 percent of market value.

faqs.q: When are Gloucester County real estate taxes due?
faqs.a: June 30 and December 5. In 2026 the December due date moved to December 7 because December 5 falls on a weekend.

faqs.q: What is the penalty for paying late in Gloucester County?
faqs.a: The county charges a 10 percent penalty after the due date, plus interest at 10 percent a year on unpaid balances.

faqs.q: How often does Gloucester County reassess real estate?
faqs.a: Every three years. The county lists reassessment documents for 2023 and 2026.

faqs.q: Where do I file a Gloucester County assessment appeal?
faqs.a: Start with an administrative review at the Real Estate Assessment office, then the Board of Equalization, then the Circuit Court. The reassessment notice lists the deadlines.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Gloucester County house with unpaid taxes?
faqs.a: Yes. The tax lien is paid from the sale proceeds at closing, so get a payoff figure from the Treasurer first.
